text:
alex: Customer hitting intermittent 500s on /v1/embeddings, screenshot doesn't show any request id. Can someone post a short checklist to ask the customer for — request token, HAR, or a minimal curl? cc @maria

maria: Sure — short checklist below, send this to the customer copy/paste-style. Also ask for the exact timestamp of the failing request.

maria: Browser (web app) quick: open DevTools -> Network -> reproduce -> click the failing request -> Headers. Look for any of these header names: `x-redwood-req`, `x-rw-request`, `x-request-id`, or `x-rw-trace`. If they see it, paste the value. If not, export HAR and include the timestamp.

maria: Mobile (iOS): enable SDK debug logs (SDK -> Settings -> verbose), reproduce, then share logs. The SDK prints lines like `RWReq: id=abcd1234 status=500` or `requestId=abcd1234`. Android: Logcat filter `Redwood` or `RWRequest` — the log line includes request id.

maria: If customer can't collect logs, ask for a minimal curl that hits the same backend and the exact client time window (UTC). Provide this curl snippet to them to run locally and mail back the output: 

maria: ```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_KEY>" \n  -d '{"input": "short test"}'
```

maria: If they can, tell them to add a request id header to the curl so we can correlate (we accept custom id headers in debug mode): `-H "x-redwood-customer-req: my-local-test-123"`.

alex: Good. What about cases where a corporate proxy strips headers?

tim: Proxy stripping is common. Ask the customer to check upstream proxy logs for `x-redwood-` headers or to temporarily bypass the proxy. If they can't bypass, ask for the full upstream request/response pair or the gateway logs — timestamped. Also ask for the client-to-proxy and proxy-to-api timestamps.

jess: For customers on Redwood Console: Support -> Debug bundles -> Generate debug token (if they have permissions). That bundle gives us request traces and host-level logs. If they don't have access, ask for a screenshot of the Console request inspector around the failure time (Network tab equivalent).

alex: How should we phrase the ask to non-technical contacts?

maria: Concise template for non-devs: 

maria: "Hi — we're investigating your error. Can you please: 1) Reproduce the error and copy the exact time (to the minute) 2) From the app, open Settings -> Support -> Export debug (or open Developer Tools -> Network -> export HAR) 3) Run this small curl and paste the output: (paste curl snippet above). If you see any header starting with `x-redwood-`, please copy that value. If you need help, we can schedule a quick remote session."

alex: Perfect. Add the bit about scrubbing secrets.

maria: Right: remind them to remove API keys from screenshots and to redact the "Authorization" header before sending. We only need the request id values and timestamps.

support-bot: Automated note: when you upload a HAR or debug bundle, please attach it to the support ticket and mark it `REQ-CORR`. The support system will auto-link the file to our tracer.

tim: One more correlation trick — ask them to send both the client-local timestamp and the server-reported Date header from the response (if any). Time skew helps us pinpoint the span in our logs.

jess: If we get a request id like `abcd1234`, here's the internal quick-check we run: `grep abcd1234 /var/log/redwood/requests*` then follow spans in tracing dashboard (trace id -> root span -> downstream). If you don't have access, attach the id in the ticket and tag `eng-oncall`.

alex: Example thread for the customer to copy (single message they can paste):

alex: "Hi Redwood support — I got a 500 from embeddings at 2026-03-15T14:02 UTC. I exported a HAR and ran your curl. I couldn't find a header named `x-redwood-req` in the network tab. HAR attached. Test curl used: (paste curl). Let me know if you need the SDK logs."

maria: Thanks — that'll make triage fast. If the customer returns only the curl output (no request id), we can still search by client IP / user-agent / exact minute window, but it takes longer. Always prioritize request id + timestamp + HAR.

alex: Closing note: add a flag in the ticket `needs-debug-token` if they can't produce a request id and we need to request a bundle from the Console team. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: File upload reminder: please use the ticket attachment flow; do not paste HAR contents inline in Slack.
